observations: Four blue metal drums stacked two-high in two groups of two, photographed outdoors on bare ground against a rough plastered wall.
Drums have visible wear, scratches, paint chipping and some rust streaks on the body.
White text 'POWEROIL' is legibly printed on the drum bodies in both photo 0 and photo 1.
Each drum has a white paper label stuck to the top lid, but the text on these labels is too small/blurred to read in either photo.
Bung caps (fill/vent plugs) are visible and closed on the top of each drum in photo 1.
No liquid, spill, or fill-level indicator is visible anywhere in either photo.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI / GIFTED TOOLS VENTURES' overlays photo 1.
A tire and a cardboard box (partly labelled, unreadable) are visible in the background, suggesting a mixed-goods yard/warehouse, not a branded oil depot.

claims.evidence: Brand name 'POWEROIL' is printed on the drums (photo 0, photo 1), but nothing shows the drums are factory-sealed/original versus reused/refilled containers; no seal, cap tamper-ring, or manufacturer batch sticker is readable.
No scale, measurement, or capacity marking is legible in either photo; standard industrial drums are commonly 200L but this is an assumption, not a read fact.

claims.claim: Correct for hydraulic, lubricant and industrial use
claims.evidence: No label content, oil grade, or viscosity marking is readable in any photo; cannot confirm intended use or that contents match the drum print.

claims.claim: Implied that drums are full of oil (product being sold as oil)
claims.evidence: Caps are shut, no liquid or weight cues (no tilt, no condensation, no drip marks) visible in photo 0 or photo 1 to confirm drums are filled rather than empty containers.

risks.risk: Drums could be empty (sold as used containers) rather than filled with oil, which would be a completely different value proposition.
risks.proof: A photo/video of an open bung with oil visibly at the top, or oil being poured out, or a clear weight/tilt test showing liquid shifting inside.
risks.if_unproven: priced as empty drums (container value only, no oil content)

risks.risk: Drums may be reconditioned/repainted and relabeled with a brand sticker rather than genuine Poweroil product, i.e. 'original' claim could be false.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of a manufacturer's embossed/stamped batch code on the drum rim or bottom, and a matching readable top label.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic used industrial drum, not as verified genuine Poweroil product

risks.risk: Rust or internal corrosion from outdoor dirt storage could compromise seal integrity or contaminate contents.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the drum interior (via open bung) and the base/rim for rust-through or pitting.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming moderate rust risk, as-is condition

risks.risk: Capacity may not actually be 200 litres as claimed.
risks.proof: A tape-measure shot against the drum height/diameter, or a visible capacity stamp on the drum body.
risks.if_unproven: priced using the smallest commonly sold industrial drum size as a conservative base, not assumed at 200L premium

proof_requests: Open one bung and show the oil level/liquid inside, or show the drum being filled/poured, to prove it is not empty.
Close-up of any embossed manufacturer stamp, batch code, or date on the drum rim/base to support 'original Poweroil' claim.
A tape measure or known-size object next to a drum to confirm the 200 litre capacity claim.
Close-up of the paper labels on top so text/grade can actually be read.
response.reason: The item type and brand print are visible, but the core value driver — whether the drums actually contain oil or are empty containers — cannot be confirmed from the photos, so it must be priced at the worst case (empty drum/container value) pending proof of filled contents and authenticity.
